expectations.text: Hafid begins as a camel boy for the merchant Pathros
He is sent to Bethlehem to sell a robe and gives it to warm a newborn infant in a cave
expectations.evidence: Robe to baby in Bethlehem cave

expectations.text: A bright star follows him, which Pathros recognizes as a sign and gives him the ten scrolls
As an old man in Damascus Hafid gives away his wealth and confides in his bookkeeper Erasmus
The scrolls go to Paul (Saul of Tarsus)
Paul brings the robe (marked by Tola/Pathros) that Hafid had given away
